newsitem.title: UK: Dollar rally fizzles in late Europe, dlr ends down.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rally fizzles in late Europe, dlr ends down.

text.p: The dollar's assault on the mark and yen faltered in late Europe as the focus shifted to the U.S trade deficit with Japan and hefty gains clocked up on rate hike speculation were eroded by profit-taking.

The dollar, which rocketed to session highs of 1.6946 marks and 123.73 yen after comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, was down nearly one pfennig at 1.6830/40 marks from Thursday's close at 1.6905/10. Dollar/yen was down at 122.40 yen at 1536 GMT from 123.61/66 in late Europe.
"The dollar has come under pressure after long positions were built up," said a trader at a U.K. bank.
Dealers, however, said they expected the dollar to remain supported ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting as markets bet the Fed would hike rates for the first time in two years.
"The dollar should remain well supported ahead of the FOMC meeting," said a trader at a U.S. bank.

Greenspan, in his testimony to the Joint Economic Committee, acknowledged on Thursday a current benign inflation outlook in the U.S. but highlighted the potential of future inflation and reiterated the Federal Reserve's pre-emptive stance on monetary policy.
Against the yen, the dollar stumbled in Europe to session lows of 122.35 yen after U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky warned Japan on Friday not to "export its way" out of recession.
"I am concerned that Japan not think that it's going to export its way out of recession, particularly with respect to significant increases in exports to the U.S.," said Barshefsky.

Analysts took the comments to mean that the only way to address the U.S-Japan trade deficit, which edged up 0.7 percent in January to $4.29 billion, was through the parity between the U.S. unit and the Japanese yen.

"Inevitably there will be an upwards flurry of the Japanese currency on concern the Bank of Japan, perhaps in conjunction with the U.S. authorities, will act to intervene to push up the currency specifically in regard to the deficit," said Julian Fisher, Japan economist, at Daiwa Europe.
But he said it was unlikely that these political considerations would have any long-term effect.

Traders said dollar/yen spike lower also weighed on dollar/mark. In late Europe the mark was above its worst levels on crosses, with mark/lira re-claiming 1,000 lire after having struggled below for most of the European session.
Sterling was off its highs at 2.7000/10 marks in late Europe after dollar/mark's boost sparked sterling's push to session highs at 2.7108 marks.
